newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Samurai to boost S.African reserves again in June.
newsitem.headline: Samurai to boost S.African reserves again in June.

text.p: South Africa will get a further boost to already record reserves this month following Tuesday's launch of a 40 billion yen samurai bond in Tokyo with a pay date of June 17.
The yen issue had been expected, but the timing caught some in the market by surprise. Many had only expected the issue in August when funds would be needed.
In fact, the issue will contribute a further 1.54 billion rand to the central bank's June reserves.

Reserves of gold and foreign exchange surged 51 percent to a record high of 21.8 billion rand in May, boosted both by inflows from the part privatisation of telecommunications concern Telkom and strong foreign demand for South African stocks and bonds.

The leap in official reserves -- well ahead of the consensus forecast of 17.7 billion -- lifts South Africa's import cover to more than two months for the first time since the rand crisis broke early last year.

The increase provides a valuable buffer as South Africa heads into the next phase of exchange control liberalisation which will allow individuals to invest offshore or hold foreign currency bank accounts for the first time since July 1.
